# API Keys & OAuth

Create an OAuth app for Close so your integration can securely connect to Close accounts. Full instructions are in the [Close developer docs.](https://developer.close.com/integrations/create-an-oauth-app)

There are two main ways to authorize (connect) your Close organization to third-party applications or your own internal system:

- using API keys
- using OAuth access

Both methods are designed to help you automate and sync your sales process with other platforms while maintaining high levels of security and data privacy. Whether a third-party app uses an API key or OAuth to connect to Close depends on how the app’s developers decided to set it up.

## API keys

An API key is a **secret token** (like a password) which you can use to connect Close data to third-party applications or your own internal system.

API keys are created and managed on a per-user basis in Close, and each key is tied to the specific Close user who created it. If that Close user is removed/deactivated, any API keys issued for them will be disabled.

### Creating an API key

To create a new API key, go to **Settings > Developer > API Keys** and click **+ New API Key**. Select the Permissions and click Create.

If you’re seeing authentication failures in an integration, double-check in **Settings > Developer > API Keys** that the API key you’re using is active. If a key was deleted, copied incorrectly, or otherwise compromised, create a new key and update the integration (this is also a common reason to rotate keys).

Make sure to give your new API key an informative name so that you’ll be able to easily tell which key is used for which integration. Once done, you’ll be given the newly-generated API key, which you should copy and store securely. This key will not be displayed ever again (only the key’s ID will be shown), so make sure to copy it.

![Developer API Keys settings page with empty list and centered New API Key button.](https://close-prd-help-docs.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/integrations/api-keys-oauth/developer_api_keys_3bd2f2.gif)

API keys vs IDs

An API key is a secret token, which is used to authenticate your requests to the Close API. It should be kept private and stored securely. On the other hand, an ID of an API key is just an identifier. It is safe to share.
 Don’t be confused by the similarity between the two. For example:

API key ID: `api_7b8KOSMa0OevK9qJvT6F9s`

API key: `api_7b8KOSMa0OevK9qJvT6F9s.2H3Bt8ktGaQ9kVK45P7j7p` *(note: not a real key)*
 The API key contains the ID, but it also contains a second secret part. Don’t ever share the full API key!

### Access Levels

An access level limits what an API key can do.

| Access Level | What the key can do |
|---|---|
| **Read only** | View Close data, but not change it. |
| **Read, write, and delete** | View, create, update, and delete Close data. |

![Developer role settings showing Manage own API keys toggle and a Maximum access level dropdown set to Read only.](https://help.close.com/_fern-files/_img/061cd16a823e9cadb53e44cd6fcf5fdf76c08fb025a03a5033ac13c7dd6b8750.webp)

Close checks the access level on every API request and rejects operations outside it. A key can never do more than its owner: it follows the owner’s role and lead visibility, and its access level narrows that access further.

Keys created before access levels were introduced keep **Read, write, and delete** access and continue to work.

**Can’t choose an access level?** Your role sets the maximum access level for your keys. Ask an admin about your role if you need a different level.

### Editing an API key

To rename a key or change its access level, click the **…** next to the key and choose **Edit**. Only the key’s owner can rename it or change its access level. You can select only an access level your role allows.

### Disabling and enabling an API key

To pause a key without deleting it, click the **…** next to the key and choose **Disable**. Integrations using the key immediately lose access.

![Developer settings page demonstrating how to disable an active API key.](https://close-prd-help-docs.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/integrations/api-keys-oauth/developer_api_keys_66ee16.gif)

To turn the key back on, click **Disabled** at the top of the list, then click the **…** next to the key and choose **Enable**.

![Developer settings page demonstrating how to access Disabled API Keys and enable them.](https://close-prd-help-docs.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/integrations/api-keys-oauth/developer_api_keys_0a7df4.gif)

Can't enable a key?

If your role no longer includes Manage own API keys, ask an admin or someone with Manage all API keys to enable it. If you still have Manage own API keys, you can enable an existing key even if its access level exceeds your role’s maximum.

### Deleting an API key

To delete an API key, click on the ”…” next to the API key you’d like to delete.

Note that deleting an API key will immediately cut off access to Close data from any integration using that key. You will not be able to restore a deleted API key. Disable it instead if you might need it again.

### Reviewing existing API keys

The API Keys list shows each key’s name and ID, owner, access level, creation date, and approximately when it was last used. Hover over **Last used** to see the recorded IP address and user agent. Usage details update at most about once an hour, so they may not reflect the latest request.

![Developer settings page showing a list of API keys with a New API key button and a tooltip for last used details.](https://help.close.com/_fern-files/_img/a7b54e3da3a1b162b23dab8d9eda5d6ba00dd3b5b1d760b68eee5b3758852693.webp)

API key access is controlled by two permissions in the **Developer** section of **Settings > Team > Roles**. For more on roles, see [Roles & Permissions](https://help.close.com/account-management/roles-permissions).

- **Manage own API keys:** Create keys and change their access levels, up to the role’s **Maximum access level**. Without this permission, you don’t see **+ New API key** and can’t enable your own disabled keys. You can still rename, disable, or delete your existing keys.
- **Manage all API keys:** View, disable, enable, and delete API keys in your organization, including keys other people created. Enabling this permission also enables and requires **Manage own API keys**.

![Developer role settings showing toggles for managing own API keys and maximum access level set to Read only.](https://help.close.com/_fern-files/_img/57c8d40d031d73111249b7e362025f0e2420bb0373beee01a1882f97fe0543e9.webp)

The predefined roles have these permissions:

| Role | Manage own API keys | Manage all API keys |
|---|---|---|
| Admin | Yes, up to Read, write, and delete | Yes |
| Super User | Yes, up to Read, write, and delete | Yes |
| User | Yes, up to Read, write, and delete | No |
| Restricted User | Yes, Read only | No |

You can configure these permissions on custom roles. For example, you can create a role that can create only **Read only** keys.

Lowering a role's maximum access level

Existing keys above the new maximum stay active. Close warns you before you save. To reduce their access, ask each owner to edit their key, or disable or delete the keys.

### Security

API keys are a great way to connect Close to your favorite applications or your own internal system. However, with great power comes great responsibility. **API keys can read and modify all of your CRM data and should be handled very carefully.**

You should always store your API keys securely and you should never share them with parties you don’t trust. It is also recommended that you periodically create new API keys, update your integration(s), and delete the old API keys. This practice is typically referred to as “rotating” your API keys.

### User availability (rep visibility)

There is no separate Close account setting to “turn on” rep visibility for integrations. Availability/visibility is provided via the User Availability endpoint, and whether you can access it depends on whether the API key or OAuth token you’re using has access to the organization.

## OAuth access

Third-party apps can use OAuth to request access to your Close organization, which involves a process where you can approve or deny the specific app’s access to your Close data, rather than handling API keys directly.

### Allowing OAuth access

To give a third-party app permission to access your Close account, navigate to the app and look for an option that says something like **Connect to Close CRM**. Selecting this will take you to a Close authorization page where you can approve the connection:

![OAuth consent dialog asking to grant Zapier access to a Close organization with permissions and Allow/Cancel buttons.](https://help.close.com/_fern-files/_img/0e70f8fec20ebb43e91152312922078a8b93afd57482c28054a22d378be1c7ef.webp)

Once allowed, the third party app will get full read/write access to your Close organization (as determined by your Close role in case you’re not a Close Admin).

OAuth authorizations are also tied to a specific Close user account. If that user is removed/deactivated, any OAuth tokens issued for them will be disabled.

Google Workspace (policy_enforced) OAuth errors

If you’re connecting Close via OAuth and see a `policy_enforced` error, your Google Workspace administrator may be blocking third-party app access. A Workspace admin will need to approve/allow the permissions requested by Close in the Google Admin console for the connection to succeed.

Can I change the scope (permissions) of the access?

No. Currently, any third-party app using OAuth will obtain the same full access to your Close account as it would with an API key.

### Revoking OAuth access

To revoke OAuth access to some of third party apps, go to your **Settings > Accounts & Apps > Authorized Apps** and click **Revoke Access…**

![Accounts & Apps Authorized Apps list showing Zapier with a Revoke Access button.](https://help.close.com/_fern-files/_img/dd71da5cd65fb3ddeb27e49f2be02ac039c46c09075a56735ac7b1519729c4fc.webp)

Note that revoking an OAuth access will immediately cut off access to Close data to that integration. The only way to restore the access it go to the third party app and request an access again.
